name: workqueue-lease-branches
description: Lease beside the core's Branches (D32, amended) on one type: Branches points its release pointer with releaseCommit, so Lease keeps release, which ends a lease, and a type composes both. Each runs its own operation, and Lease's guard holds Branches' writes to the holder as it holds any writing operation.

base.description: The commit its rows lay over: its parent's head when it was branched or last rebased; null for none.

createdAt.description: When it was created, a date-time in UTC.

createdBy.description: The subject of the caller who created it.

head.description: Its latest commit; null before its first.

id.description: Its id, a UUID in its canonical form.

name.description: Its name, unique among the instance's live refs.

parent.description: The ref it was branched from; null for the primary line.

sealed.description: Whether it is sealed, so it takes no more writes.

updatedAt.description: When it was last written, a date-time in UTC.

updatedBy.description: The subject of the caller who last wrote it.

version.description: Its version, which every write through it names and moves on.

s2.description: The ref at its new version, and the commit written.

commit.description: The commit written; null when there was nothing to commit.

s3.description: How to settle conflicts, by kind, entity key and unit path: take a side's value (take) or give one (value, null included).

commit.description: The commit written; null when there was nothing to commit.

base.description: The unit's value at the merge base; absent where it is absent.

ours.description: The unit's value on the side merged into.

oursAuthor.description: The subject who last wrote our side's row.

path.description: A JSON Pointer to the unit in the row; empty for an edit against a delete.

theirs.description: The unit's value on the side merged from.

theirsAuthor.description: The subject who last wrote their side's row.

s5.description: A tree, its content hash and what was found wrong in it.

contentHash.description: The SHA-256 of the tree's content, as lowercase hex.

findings.description: What compose found wrong in the tree; none for a commit's.

tree.description: The tree: by kind, its rows, each with its role, audit and content columns, an actor as a subject.

scenarios.name: Lease beside Branches (node) > a type composes both: Lease's release ends the lease and Branches' releaseCommit moves the release pointer

declaration.name: Lease
declaration.description: An exclusive, time-bounded lease on the instance, held by one principal and numbered by a fencing token that advances at every acquire, release and expiry. While the lease is active only its holder may change the instance, and a write that presents a token other than the current one, as Lease's precondition, is refused whoever calls; a heartbeat with the current token renews the lease and delivers the directives sent to the holder. A lease its holder stops renewing expires, and the expiry can move the instance's Workflow status back.

acquirePermission.description: The permission a principal needs to acquire a lease. Absent, any principal who may write the instance can.

directOn.description: Directives the engine's runner sends the holder of an instance's active lease when the target of one of the instance's links moves on: a new revision of Revisions, or a release of Branches; for a pinned link, a revision tells only the instances the target moved past. The runner sends each with direct, as its principal, which needs directPermission, or overridePermission when that is absent, once per lease and move (dedupeKey). An instance with no lease held hears nothing, and its next holder nothing either. Needs Links on the type; one entry per link.

data.description: Its data, beside revised, which the runner sets: the link, the target's schema and id, and its revision or the release's commit.

name.description: The directive's name, as direct takes it.

revised.description: The link whose target's move sends the directive.

link.description: A link of the type's Links config.

directPermission.description: The permission a principal needs to send the holder a directive; overridePermission when absent. With neither, direct is refused.

escalate.description: Used instead of onExpiry at the expiry or abandon that reaches maxExpiries, which it needs. Needs Workflow on the type.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other state it stays.

transition.description: The state to move to, through Workflow's transition.

exempt.description: Writing operations of the type's other behaviors, each as <Behavior>.<operation>, that a principal other than the holder may run while the lease is active, and that requireToken does not hold to the token.

heartbeatMs.description: How often the holder should send a heartbeat, in milliseconds, at most half of ttlMs, so one late heartbeat does not lose the lease; a third of ttlMs when absent. acquire returns it.

maxExpiries.description: How many expiries an instance may have, abandons included. Once it has had this many, its lease cannot be acquired again until resetExpiries.

maxHoldField.description: An integer field of the type that gives the instance's own longest hold, in milliseconds. When the instance holds a positive integer there, it overrides maxHoldMs.

maxHoldMs.description: The longest a principal may hold a lease after acquiring it, in milliseconds, renewed or not; no limit when absent.

onExpiry.description: Moves the instance's Workflow status when a lease ends with the work unfinished: at an expiry, an abandon and a release, while the status is one of from. Needs Workflow on the type.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other state it stays.

transition.description: The state to move to, through Workflow's transition.

overridePermission.description: The permission that lets a principal release another principal's lease, change the instance while another principal holds its lease, reset its expiries, and send directives when directPermission is absent.

requireToken.description: When true, a write to an instance with an active lease that does not present the current token as Lease's precondition is refused, the holder's own included, so every process of a principal fences its writes. Exempt and read-only operations, Lease's own operations and a principal with overridePermission are not held to it.

sweepMs.description: How often the engine's runner expires the leases past their expiry time or longest hold, in milliseconds; 5000 when absent.

ttlMs.description: How long a lease lasts after its acquire or its last heartbeat, in milliseconds; 60000 when absent.

fields.name: holder
fields.description: The subject of the principal that holds the lease; absent when the instance is free.

fields.name: token
fields.description: The fencing token. It advances at every acquire, release and expiry, and a write under the lease presents it.

fields.name: acquiredAt
fields.description: When the lease was acquired, in epoch milliseconds; absent when the instance is free.

fields.name: renewedAt
fields.description: Its acquire or its last heartbeat, in epoch milliseconds; absent when the instance is free.

fields.name: expiresAt
fields.description: When the lease expires unless it is renewed, in epoch milliseconds; absent when the instance is free.

fields.name: active
fields.description: Whether a lease is held and has not expired.

fields.name: expiries
fields.description: How many leases have expired or been abandoned since the last resetExpiries.

fields.name: ended
fields.description: How and when the last lease ended (reason and at); absent while one is held.

operations.name: acquire
operations.description: Takes the lease for the caller and returns its fencing token. Refused while a lease is active, the caller's own included (heartbeat renews it), without acquirePermission when the config names one, and once the instance has had maxExpiries expiries. Over a lease that expired, it applies that expiry first.

ttlMs.description: How long the lease lasts after its acquire and each heartbeat, in milliseconds, at most the config's ttlMs; the config's when absent.

expiresAt.description: When the lease expires unless renewed, in epoch milliseconds.

heartbeatMs.description: How often to send a heartbeat, in milliseconds.

token.description: The lease's fencing token, which the holder's writes present as Lease's precondition.

operations.name: heartbeat
operations.description: Renews the lease, never past its longest hold, acknowledges the directives acknowledge names, and returns the directives sent under it that are not acknowledged. Only the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition, while the lease is active: an expired lease cannot be renewed.

acknowledge.description: Directives of the lease to mark handled first, as acknowledge does, so a heartbeat acknowledges in the same write; empty, none.

directives.description: The directives sent under this lease and not acknowledged, oldest first.

dedupeKey.description: The key it was sent with, when it was.

id.description: The directive's number in its lease.

expiresAt.description: When the lease now expires unless renewed, in epoch milliseconds.

operations.name: release
operations.description: Ends an active lease: the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition, or a principal with overridePermission, who need not. The token advances, so the directives sent under the lease are not delivered again, and onExpiry moves the status when it is still one of its from states. With abandon, the holder gives the work up as failed: the release counts as an expiry, and escalate applies at the one that reaches maxExpiries.

abandon.description: Whether the work is given up as failed, so the release counts as an expiry.

operations.name: expire
operations.description: Applies the expiry of a lease past its expiry time or its longest hold: the holder is cleared, the token advances, the expiry is counted unless the instance is in a terminal state of its Workflow, and onExpiry or escalate moves the status. Any principal who may write the instance may call it; on any other instance it changes nothing. With holder, a principal with overridePermission expires that holder's lease at once, active or not, unless notRenewedAfter spares it. The engine's runner calls it on every lapsed lease, every sweepMs.

holder.description: The principal whose lease to expire now, active or not; it needs overridePermission.

notRenewedAfter.description: With holder: an active lease its holder acquired or renewed after this time, in epoch milliseconds, is spared, since its own heartbeats show the process holding it is alive. A lapsed one expires all the same.

reason.description: Why, when one expired: ttl, its holder stopped renewing it; maxHold, it reached its longest hold; holder, it was active and expired by its holder's name.

operations.name: direct
operations.description: Sends the holder of the active lease a directive, which its heartbeats deliver until it acknowledges it. With dedupeKey, a directive already sent under the lease with the key is not sent again. A principal needs directPermission, or overridePermission when that is absent, and is refused when the config names neither; another behavior of the type sends one with call(), as the principal it runs for, without either.

dedupeKey.description: Sends the directive once per lease: when one was sent under the current token with this key, acknowledged or not, that one stands and nothing is sent.

created.description: Whether this call sent it; false when one with dedupeKey was already sent.

id.description: The directive's number in its lease: the one sent, or the one already sent with dedupeKey.

operations.name: acknowledge
operations.description: Marks directives of the lease as handled, so heartbeats stop delivering them. Only the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition.

operations.name: expireHolder
operations.description: Expires every lease one principal holds on the schema's instances, active or not, as expire with that holder does on each: for a principal that is gone. With notRenewedAfter, an active lease renewed after that time is spared. Needs overridePermission; refused when the config names none.

holder.description: The principal whose leases to expire.

notRenewedAfter.description: As expire's: an active lease acquired or renewed after this time is spared.

ids.description: The instances whose lease expired, by id.

reasons.description: How many expired for each reason expire gives, by reason; a reason none expired for is absent.

operations.name: resetExpiries
operations.description: Sets the instance's count of expiries back to 0, so a lease can be acquired again after maxExpiries. Needs overridePermission; refused when the config names none.

token.description: The lease's current fencing token, as acquire returned it: a write that presents another is refused (token_stale).

vetoes.description: Another principal holds the instance's active lease.
The caller already holds the active lease: acquire refuses it, and heartbeat renews it.
No principal holds a lease on the instance.
The caller does not hold the lease the call needs it to hold.
The lease is past its expiry time or its longest hold: it gives its holder nothing, and only its expiry can follow.
The token the call presents as Lease's precondition is not the lease's current one: a newer lease, or none, has replaced the one it names.
The call presents no token as Lease's precondition, and needs one: a heartbeat, an acknowledgement or a holder's release, or any write under requireToken while the lease is active.
The instance has had maxExpiries expiries, so its lease cannot be acquired until resetExpiries.
maxHoldField cannot change while a lease is held.
The config names no permission that allows the call: direct without directPermission or overridePermission, resetExpiries without overridePermission.

declaration.name: Branches
declaration.description: Makes each instance the root of a version graph: refs, a primary line and drafts of it, over rows of the kinds the config names, each kind's content a type of the schema document; commits, merges, rebases and reverts; and a release pointer whose history is the release log, its version the release field. The instance's own fields stay outside the graph. The graph lives in the behavior's own tables, and deleting the instance deletes it. With sweep in its config, a schedule discards idle drafts and keeps the graph's storage in bounds.

order.description: The kind's integer field that orders siblings, as @graphMember's order.

parent.description: Containment, as @graphMember's parent: key is the kind's field, of a UUID scalar, that holds the parent row's entity key, and of is the parent's kind, this one included. Deleting a parent removes its descendants.

retentionDays.description: How many days of the kind's history the sweep keeps, as @versioned's retentionDays; all of it when absent.

singleton.description: At most one live row of the kind, as @graphMember's singleton.

type.description: The type of the schema document, besides the instance type, whose fields are the kind's content.

units.description: A field's conflict unit, as @conflictUnit sets it: atomic (the default), keyed (each top-level key of a JSON object), jsonSchema, or excluded (not content: never merged or hashed).

kinds.description: The graph's kinds, by name: camelCase, at most 64 characters.

primary.description: The name of each instance's primary line; main when absent.

snapshotEvery.description: How many commits past the nearest snapshot on its chain a commit is snapshotted at, as @versionGraph's snapshotEvery; 64 when absent.

sweep.description: Turns the sweep schedule on for the schema: each run discards the drafts idle past abandonAfter, then deletes the rows of refs discarded longer ago than discardGrace, prunes each kind's history past its retentionDays and writes missing snapshots.

abandonAfter.description: Discards a draft with no write for this many milliseconds; none when absent.

discardGrace.description: How long a discarded ref's rows are kept, in milliseconds; seven days when absent.

intervalMs.description: How often it runs, in milliseconds; at least 1000.

pruneBatch.description: At most this many history images of each kind pruned per run; no limit when absent.

fields.name: release
fields.description: The number of the instance's latest release: the release pointer's version, which releaseCommit names to move it. Absent before the first release.

operations.name: branch
operations.description: Creates a draft of a ref of the instance, its primary line or another draft, whose rows lay over the ref's head. Without fromRef it branches from the primary line, which an instance created before its schema composed Branches gets then.

fromRef.description: The ref to branch from, by id; the instance's primary line when absent.

name.description: The draft's name, unique among the instance's live refs.

operations.name: save
operations.description: Writes rows on a draft, at its version: by kind, each upsert row is an entity's whole content and, to replace an entity the draft reads, its entity_key, and is checked against the kind's type; each delete removes an entity from the draft; each unset drops the draft's own row of an entity, so the draft reads it through its base again. A primary line takes no save: work merges into it.

delete.description: Entity keys of entities the draft reads.

unset.description: Entity keys of entities the draft has rows of its own for.

upsert.description: Rows: entity_key and the kind's fields.

edits.description: The edits by kind: upserts, then deletes, then unsets, kind by kind.

resultSchema.description: The draft at its new version, and the rows the upserts stored.

saved.description: By kind, each upsert's row as stored, in edit order.

operations.name: commit
operations.description: Commits a draft at its version: what it composes to that its last commit, or its base, does not. A tagged commit takes the instance's next sequence, and only a tagged commit can be released.

tag.description: Whether the commit takes the instance's next sequence.

resultSchema.description: The draft at its new version, and the commit.

commit.description: The commit written; null when there was nothing to commit.

operations.name: seal
operations.description: Commits a draft at its version when it has changes, and seals it: it takes no more writes.

operations.name: merge
operations.description: Merges a ref's head into another ref of the instance at its version, against the source's base: an entity or a unit changed on one side takes that side, and one changed differently on both is a conflict. With conflicts left after the resolutions it writes nothing and returns them; otherwise it writes the result onto the target and commits it. Merge is the only write a primary line takes.

source.description: The ref to merge from, by id.

tag.description: Whether the commit takes the instance's next sequence.

target.description: The ref to merge into, by id.

resultSchema.description: The ref merged into, and the commit written; with conflicts nothing was written, the ref is as it was and the commit is null.

operations.name: rebase
operations.description: Moves a draft at its version onto its parent's head: merges the parent's head into the draft, its uncommitted work included, against the draft's base, and commits on the draft. With conflicts left after the resolutions it writes nothing and returns them.

resultSchema.description: The draft, and the commit written; with conflicts nothing was written.

operations.name: revert
operations.description: Writes the rows that make a draft at its version compose to an earlier commit's tree, and commits them. History is never rewritten.

toCommit.description: The commit of the instance whose tree the draft takes, by id.

operations.name: releaseCommit
operations.description: Points the instance's release pointer at a tagged commit of the instance, fenced by the pointer's version, 0 for the first release: the version graph's release, named so a type can compose Branches with Lease, whose release ends a lease. It writes no rows: a rollback is a releaseCommit of an earlier tagged commit, and the pointer's history is the release log.

version.description: The release pointer's version; 0 for the instance's first release.
Its version, which the next releaseCommit names.

operations.name: discard
operations.description: Discards a draft at its version, which frees its name. The sweep deletes a discarded draft's rows once its grace has passed; its commits stay. The primary line is not discarded.

operations.name: refs
operations.description: Lists the instance's live refs, its primary line first, in the order they were created, one page at a time.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many refs; 50 when absent.

items.description: A ref: the instance's primary line or a draft of it.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: releases
operations.description: Lists the instance's release log, oldest first, one page at a time: each version of its release pointer, the commit it named and who released it when.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many releases; 50 when absent.

releasedBy.description: The subject of the caller who released it.

version.description: The pointer's version: 1 for the first release.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: compose
operations.description: Reads a ref's tree: its base commit's tree with the ref's own rows laid over it, uncommitted work included.

operations.name: materialize
operations.description: Reads a commit's tree.

operations.name: released
operations.description: Reads the instance's release pointer and the tree of the commit it names. An instance never released has none (not_found).

resultSchema.description: The release pointer and its commit's tree.

contentHash.description: The SHA-256 of the tree's content, as lowercase hex.

findings.description: What compose found wrong in the tree; none for a commit's.

version.description: Its version, which the next releaseCommit names.

tree.description: The tree: by kind, its rows, each with its role, audit and content columns, an actor as a subject.

operations.name: diff
operations.description: Lists the entities the trees of two commits of the instance differ on.

row.description: The later tree's row: its tombstone for a DELETE, when it has one.

operations.name: history
operations.description: Lists the commits a ref wrote, newest first.

contentHash.description: The SHA-256 of its tree's content, as lowercase hex.

createdAt.description: When it was written, a date-time in UTC.

createdBy.description: The subject of the caller who wrote it.

id.description: Its id, a UUID in its canonical form.

parent.description: The commit before it on its ref's chain; null for none.

ref.description: The ref it was written on.

sequence.description: Its number among the instance's tagged commits, 1, 2, 3, ...; null for an untagged commit.

snapshot.description: Whether its full set of row versions is stored, so a read of its tree stops there.

vetoes.description: A write through a ref, or a releaseCommit, at a version the ref or the release pointer has moved past.
branch to a name another live ref of the instance has.
A write through a sealed ref.
save, commit, seal or revert on a primary line, which takes writes only from merge.
commit of a draft that composes to the tree of its last commit, or of its base.
save that deletes an entity the draft does not read, or unsets a row the draft does not have.
A commit whose tree breaks the graph's rules (an absent parent, a second singleton, a parent cycle, an order out of range), with the findings in details.
merge of a ref into itself.
rebase of a primary line, which has no parent to rebase onto.
releaseCommit of a commit that is not tagged.
A read of a commit's tree that would walk more commits than the engine's ceiling.
discard of the instance's primary line, which its drafts branch from and merge into.
